subject: PrivDep DPA: subprocessors, geofencing controls and BYOK escrow timeline
messages:
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acmehealth.org>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.org>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PrivDep DPA: subprocessors, geofencing controls and BYOK escrow timeline

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the earlier demo — Acme's security and procurement teams reviewed the private deployment materials. A few items we need to clarify before we can move to signature:

- Full subprocessor inventory for the private deployment (we need names, roles, hosting region and whether they will see customer plaintext).
- Geofencing: can Redwood guarantee that inference processing and KV/cache copies for our tenant remain within US regions only? Any automated fallback to other regions needs to be explicitly opt-in.
- BYOK escrow: we need a short runbook describing what triggers an escrow release, who can request it, and proof-of-escrow procedures (HSM vs. file-based).
- Operator access windows and breakglass flow: we want time-bound breakglass (max 4 hours per incident), audit evidence, and a notification window of 24 hours.
- Pen test and evidence cadence: Acme asks for quarterly penetration test summaries for the private deployment environment.

Attaching our standard procurement checklist (see attachment). Can you confirm Redwood's positions and an estimated timeline for the updated DPA + inventory?

Regards,
Alice Wu
Sr. Security Manager, Acme Health
[attachment: acme_procurement_checklist_20280213.pdf (pdf)]

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acmehealth.org>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 10:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDep DPA: subprocessors, geofencing controls and BYOK escrow timeline

Hi Alice — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. High-level answers below; technical and legal team follow-up is CC'd.

- Subprocessors: we can provide a current inventory and a fortnightly notification window for changes during negotiation. We maintain a classified inventory and will deliver an export with roles and data-plane access levels.
- Geofencing: for a VPC/on-prem private deployment we can enforce region routing rules; automated fallback to other regions is off by default. We will declare the allowed regions in the DPA annex and surface any exceptions.
- BYOK escrow: Redwood supports customer-controlled keys (BYOK) with optional escrow. Escrow is HSM-backed or encrypted key-vault export (customer choice). We'll provide a runbook that lists triggers, auth checks and evidence required for a release.
- Operator breakglass: we accept a time-bound breakglass policy; proposed default is 8 hours with audit capture. Karthik, can you confirm whether we can support a 4-hour maximum for Acme and what telemetry we'll include?
- Pen tests: we can provide quarterly high-level summaries and SOC-2 style attestations; full reports remain redacted for 3P vendors but we can provide findings and mitigations.

Next steps: Laura will coordinate the DPA redline with legal and share a draft by 2028-02-14. Karthik will attach the operator access matrix and a short technical note.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
[attachment: subprocessor_inventory_20280213.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acmehealth.org>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDep DPA: subprocessors, geofencing controls and BYOK escrow timeline

Alice / Irene — quick technical clarifications and what we can deliver this week: 

- Operator access matrix: attached. Telemetry includes timestamped session recordings, operator identity, justification, and full KV-cache access logs per request. We can enforce session duration limits; Acme's ask for max 4-hour breakglass is technically enforceable. We'll emit a post-incident export with signed audit evidence.
- Geofencing: when deployed into Acme's VPC we bind egress rules to US-only AZs. If you opt for Redwood-managed control plane, we can still guarantee data-plane stays in-region; we will not enable cross-region fallback without explicit opt-in boolean in the tenant config.
- BYOK escrow mechanics: we support two flow options — HSM escrow (preferred) or encrypted key bundle held in escrow. Escrow release requires (a) authenticated legal request + (b) two Redwood ops approvals + (c) customer attestation. We can also integrate with your KMS via API for rotation proofs.

Deliverables this week (by EOD 2028-02-14): operator-access-matrix.csv, short BYOK runbook (800–1200 words), and an export of current subprocessors.

-- Karthik
Principal Infra Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: operator-access-matrix.csv (csv)]

From: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.org>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDep DPA: subprocessors, geofencing controls and BYOK escrow timeline

Thanks for the quick responses. Attached are our DPA redlines. A few legal asks that need explicit language: 

- Subprocessor notification window: we prefer 30 days' notice and a right to object for materially new subprocessors.
- Escrow release triggers: we need a clause for emergency escrow release if a lawful order is served and the customer is unable to respond within 24 hours; Redwood must provide forensic evidence of the release.
- Data egress: the DPA must state that no plaintext inference logs or KV cache are exported outside US-controlled infrastructure without express written consent.

Can Redwood provide a draft with the above points included and confirm whether the 4-hour breakglass ceiling will be contractually limited? We sent the redlines via DocuSign as well: https://docusign.com/AcmeHealth/DPA-2028

Regards,
Acme Health Legal
[attachment: dpa_redlines_acme_20280214.pdf (pdf)]

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acmehealth.org>, legal@acmehealth.org
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDep DPA: subprocessors, geofencing controls and BYOK escrow timeline

Alice / Acme legal — thanks for the redlines. Summary of our commitments and next steps: 

- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a full inventory export and accepts a 30-day notification window during the commitment period. We'll include a written right-to-object workflow in the DPA annex.
- Breakglass: Redwood will commit contractually to a 4-hour maximum operator breakglass window for this deployment; incidents beyond that window require additional customer approval and separate attestation.
- Escrow: we'll update the escrow runbook to include emergency release flow for lawful orders and the required forensic evidence chain. HSM-backed escrow will be the standard for Acme unless you request the alternate encrypted-bundle option.
- Data egress: DPA language will state no plaintext inference logs or KV-cache exports outside US-controlled infra without express written consent.

I'll circulate a clean DPA incorporating these items by end of day 2028-02-15 and schedule a 30-minute legal/technical call for 2028-02-16 10:00 AM PT so we can lock the remaining redlines. Please confirm availability.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: dpa_redlines_response_20280215.pdf (pdf)]
